data.one_liner: Hold BuildContext globally to access it anywhere in the app without passing it.
data.what_it_does: It stores the app's BuildContext globally by attaching to the root navigatorKey. Developers can then retrieve the current context, state, widget, or overlay from anywhere without explicit parameter passing.
use_when: You need access to the current BuildContext in non-widget utility or service classes.
You want to show dialogs or snackbars without passing context through multiple layers.
avoid_when: You prefer structured dependency injection or clean state management practices.
You are building apps where global context tracking can lead to anti-patterns or hard-to-debug lifecycle issues.
strengths: Extremely simple setup with a single navigatorKey assignment.
Allows accessing context from anywhere in the codebase.
weaknesses: Relies on a global state approach which is generally considered an anti-pattern in Flutter.
Can lead to using context when it might be stale or invalid.
data.setup_notes: Assign ContextHolder.key to the navigatorKey of your MaterialApp or CupertinoApp.
